current_activity: becoming operational at Rennes under Simpson
notes: Event date: Breakout-30 p636: Ninth Army became operational at Rennes on 5 September; VIII Corps passed to it five days later (see conflict group G013). Event definition: the army becomes operational. Relationship: assigned to 12th Army Group (Pogue, Supreme Command ch. 15). Location: Rennes, named by the Green Book for the headquarters; point is the town centroid.

composing_units: VIII Corps (from 10 September); 83rd Infantry Division (direct control from 10 September per CMH table); 6th Armored Division (direct control from 5-10 September, to mid-September)
current_activity: taking VIII Corps from Third Army control
notes: Event date: Breakout-30 p636: VIII Corps passed from Third Army to Ninth Army on 10 September; Ninth Army was operational at Rennes on 5 September. Event definition: Ninth Army takes over the Brest operation through VIII Corps (operational control). The 6th Armored and 83rd Divisions came directly under army control by separate decisions that the text does not date (see C0512 and C0514); they are not part of this event's date. Location: the CMH command-post list gives Ninth Army at Rennes on 8 September, two days before. Relationship: 12th Army Group assigned from 5 September. Event support: high for VIII Corps (Green Book, 10 September). Location support: moderate (command post listed two days earlier).

current_activity: takes XIX Corps from First Army and opens a command post at Maastricht
notes: Event date: 22 October 1944, noon (Siegfried p378: the Ninth Army was to open a command post at Maastricht on 22 October and at noon on that date the paper transfer of XIX Corps and supporting units was to take place; the VIII Corps passed to First Army). Event definition: Ninth Army moves from Luxembourg to the north wing between First Army and the British, taking XIX Corps north of Aachen; VIII Corps goes to First Army (see the First Army row of the same date). Relationship: 12th Army Group assigned (Breakout-30 p636; CMH tables). Location: Maastricht city centroid; the atlas list gives Maastricht from 25 October (three days after the planned date). Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Maastricht. Event support: high (Green Book states the order and the time). Location support: moderate (the opening date of the command post is planned in the Green Book and listed three days later in the atlas).

current_activity: passes to 21st Army Group under Montgomery
notes: Event date: 20 December 1944 (Ardennes p423, p425: Eisenhower's order placing First and Ninth Armies under Montgomery's command; the CMH tables for Ninth Army divisions show the British 21st Army Group attached from 20 December). The hour is not documented. Event definition: Ninth Army (with First Army) is placed under 21st Army Group; the 12th Army Group keeps Third Army. Ninth Army is also stripped of the 84th Division (leaving on 20 December) and, by the 21st, the 2nd Armored Division (Ardennes p426). Relationship: British 21st Army Group operational_control from 20 December; 12th Army Group assigned stays listed (CMH tables keep it in the assigned column). The end date, 3 April 1945 (inclusive last day), is separately sourced from the CMH tables (the 4 April 1945 row restores the 12th Army Group) and lies outside this batch window; the confidence of this December row does not apply to it. Location: Maastricht is the last-known headquarters place, not a documented position on 20 December: the atlas lists Maastricht from 25 October and nothing later until Rheydt on 11 March 1945, and the Green Book pages read do not locate the Ninth Army headquarters on 20 December; no source used moves it, so the point is the nearest earlier listed place, 56 days earlier. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Maastricht. Event support: high (Green Book narrative and CMH tables). Location support: low (a 56-day gap to the nearest list entry, no narrative for the day).
